sub_answers.sub_question: Obstructions to existence of nontrivial derivations preserving the twisting map in Hom-algebras
sub_answers.text:
Derivations must be compatible with the twisting maps, which leads to the study of α^kβ^l-generalized derivations rather than ordinary derivations [d46845s0p0].
Cohomological structures are needed to encode generalized derivation extensions, which constrains the existence of nontrivial derivations preserving the twist [d66753s0p0].
Inner-derivations and centroids must be reconsidered and explicitly computed in Hom-settings, indicating additional structural restrictions on derivations that preserve the twisting map [d84971s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Known classification difficulties or counterexamples showing failure of PBW or envelope constructions in Hom-contexts
Limitations of standard cohomology theories to detect deformations or extensions of Hom-algebras
sub_answers.text:
The cohomology theory must be adapted to the Hom-setting to study bialgebras and related deformation questions, indicating that standard cohomologies are not directly sufficient for Hom-structures [d55626s0p0].
Existence of extensions is governed by higher cohomology (notably a third cohomology obstruction), which shows that classical low-degree cohomology may miss essential extension data in Hom-contexts [d39985s0p0].
Cohomology theories have been upgraded and tailored (for example to encode generalized derivation extensions), illustrating limits of unmodified traditional cohomology for detecting Hom-deformations [d66753s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Issues in defining and classifying fiberwise Hom-structures on bundles or sheaves over base spaces
sub_answers.text:
Classifications of Hom-like structures on bundles often require surjectivity conditions on the twisting map α for certain equivalences and T^*-extension identifications [d21442s0p0].
Constructing characteristic classes via flat connections valued in infinite-dimensional Lie algebras of derivations indicates technical difficulties in defining fiberwise Hom-structures using standard connection methods [d30072s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Open problems and conjectures concerning rigidity, integrability, or classification of affine-twisted Hom-algebras
sub_answers.text:
Classification results are currently available only in low dimensions for some Hom-type algebras, evidencing difficulty in extending classifications to higher dimensions [d84971s0p0].
Cohomological obstructions, such as nontrivial classes in third cohomology, present open barriers to existence and extension problems in Hom-extensions and thus to complete classification and integrability [d39985s0p0].
The need to upgrade and adapt cohomology theories to capture generalized derivation extensions signals unresolved problems in establishing rigidity and deformation classifications for affine-twisted Hom-algebras [d66753s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Description of modules and representations of Hom-Lie algebras and changes from classical representation theory
sub_answers.text:
Modules and representations of Hom-Lie and related Hom-type algebras are defined analogously to classical representations but adapted to the Hom-structure, and categories of Hom-type algebras are closed under twisting by self-morphisms which affects module structure [d9858s0p0].
Representations of symmetric BiHom-Leibniz algebras of type B1 are explicitly defined in that setting, giving a Hom-adapted notion of module for those algebras [d46845s0p0].
Representations of algebraic structures with semisimple enveloping algebras can be described in terms of representations of the enveloping Lie algebra with additional Hom-type data, relating classical representation data to Hom-representations [d98588s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Characterization of derivation algebras (inner versus outer derivations) in Hom-type algebras
sub_answers.text:
Hom-type algebras admit families of generalized derivations parametrized by powers of the twisting maps, such as α^kβ^l-generalized derivations and α^kβ^l-quasi-derivations [d46845s0p0].
Classifications of derivations in operator-algebra contexts show that many derivations are inner in classical settings, for example every derivation of a von Neumann algebra into itself is inner, and triple derivations into itself are inner triple derivations [d20197s0p0].
Results on matrix and measurable-operator algebras establish that 2-local derivations often reduce to genuine derivations under natural hypotheses, providing rigidity results that constrain outer derivations in those frameworks [d35042s0p0][d16282s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Use of Hom-pre-Lie structures in deformation theory and explicit deformation formulas
sub_answers.text:
Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras are developed within the Hom-Lie cohomology framework and are shown to be equivalent to standard Manin triples and certain matched pairs, providing structural tools for deformation theory in the Hom setting [d55626s0p0].
A Hom-s-matrix construction yields explicit Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and facilitates construction of coboundary Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras, giving concrete formulas for deformations in many cases [d55626s0p0].
Deformation theory controlled by pre-Lie algebras supplies an integration theory and gauge actions that give explicit homotopical formulae for transferred structures, which generalize to the Hom context via analogous mechanisms [d26245s0p0].
Multi-parameter formal deformations of ternary Hom-Nambu-Lie algebras produce explicit formal deformations of standard algebraic operations such as the Jacobian determinant and cross product, illustrating explicit deformation formulas in Hom-type settings [d54668s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Role of Hom-algebra structures in geometry: connections to affine manifolds, flat connections, and fibers
sub_answers.text:
Hom-algebraic and affine structures interact with geometric connections: statistical manifolds with divisible cubic forms admit affine connections whose geodesic connectedness follows from geodesic completeness, providing geometric contexts where affine connections behave well [d106337s0p0].
Infinitesimally homogeneous affine manifolds with prescribed structure groups include flat torsion-free symplectic affine structures characterized by their group, relating algebraic structure groups to flat affine geometries [d130054s0p0].
Specialized affine connections on Hessian manifolds, such as hybrid connections, are determined by Hessian potentials and relate affine projective geometry with infinitesimal holonomy, connecting Hom-style compatibility notions to geometric fibers and connection properties [d83256s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Examples where twisting produces new Lie algebra actions or altered symmetry algebras in physical models
sub_answers.text:
Twisting by self-morphisms produces new Hom-type algebra structures such as Hom-Lie-Yamaguti algebras, thereby creating new algebraic actions and altered symmetry algebras from classical ones via the twisting procedure [d9858s0p0].
Constructions from classical Lie-Yamaguti and Malcev algebras yield Hom-versions whose binary and ternary operations can change algebraic identities and hence the realized symmetry actions in models [d9858s0p0].
Formal deformations in ternary Hom-Nambu-Lie settings produce deformed algebras like the ternary q-Virasoro-Witt algebra as formal deformations of classical Virasoro-Witt structures, exemplifying twisting/deformation producing new symmetry algebras relevant to physical models [d54668s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Definition and axioms of a Hom-Lie algebra including the twisting map and Hom-Jacobi identity
sub_answers.text: Hom-Lie algebras generalize Lie algebras in a twisted way and are mentioned alongside Hom-Lie triple systems and Hom-Nambu algebras as part of this generalization [d9858s0p0]. Hom-Lie structures form a class within hierarchies of Hom-type algebras and appear in studies that relate BiHom-Lie and Lie algebras via specialization of structure maps [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Definition and axioms of a pre-Lie algebra (left-symmetric algebra) and its relation to Lie algebras
sub_answers.text: Pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebras are algebraic structures that are closely interconnected with Lie algebras and with Rota-Baxter and O-operators in algebraic constructions [d52442s0p0]. Pre-Lie algebras appear in the same network of structures that connect Rota-Baxter operators, O-operators, and post-Lie algebras on Lie algebras [d52442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Definition and construction of an affine twist or affine action on an algebraic structure
sub_answers.text: Affine actions and affine datum are used to parametrize and realize extensions in varieties of algebras that are modules expanded by multilinear operators [d89275s0p0]. Affine ideals with unary actions determine parametrizations of extensions and are part of the framework for deconstruction and reconstruction of such extensions [d89275s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Standard examples of Hom-algebras obtained via Yau twist from associative or Lie algebras
sub_answers.text: Hom-type algebras can be constructed from classical algebras by twisting with self-morphisms, and the category of Hom-Lie-Yamaguti algebras is closed under such twisting by self-morphisms [d9858s0p0]. Constructions from classical Lie-Yamaguti algebras and from Malcev algebras are given as examples of this twisting process [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Relationship between pre-Lie algebras and their associated Lie algebras via commutator bracket
sub_answers.text: Pre-Lie algebras are linked to Lie algebras through their role in the network of algebraic structures associated with Rota-Baxter operators, O-operators, and post-Lie constructions on Lie algebras [d52442s0p0]. This interconnection places pre-Lie and post-Lie algebras in direct relation to associated Lie algebraic structures in those operator-based constructions [d52442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Formulation of the Hom-Jacobi identity and how it modifies the classical Jacobi identity
sub_answers.text: The Hom-Jacobi identity replaces the classical Jacobi identity by inserting a twisting self-map into the identity, producing a twisted Jacobi condition for Hom-Lie-type structures [d9858s0p0]. The category of Hom-Lie-Yamaguti algebras is closed under twisting by self-morphisms, which implements the modification of the Jacobi-type relations via composition with the twist map [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Expression of pre-Lie identity and its Hom-version under a twisting endomorphism
sub_answers.text: The pre-Lie identity is modified in Hom-pre-Lie contexts by composing the binary operation or its arguments with the twisting endomorphism, yielding Hom-pre-Lie identities adapted to the twist [d55626s0p0]. Constructions of Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and matched pairs use the cohomology framework for Hom-Lie algebras to encode these twisted pre-Lie relations [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Definition of derivations of Hom-algebras and how twisting affects the Leibniz rule
sub_answers.text: Derivations of Hom-algebras are defined relative to the twisting maps, leading to notions such as alpha^k beta^l-generalized derivations and quasi-derivations that incorporate powers of the structure maps into the Leibniz-type rule [d46845s0p0]. The Leibniz rule is deformed by the twist so that derivation identities include compositions with the twisting endomorphisms [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Construction of universal enveloping algebras for Hom-Lie algebras and corresponding PBW-type statements
sub_answers.text: Constructions analogous to universal enveloping algebras for Hom-Lie algebras are obtained via twisting procedures and by building Hom-type analogues of classical constructions from the untwisted algebras [d9858s0p0]. Closure of Hom-Lie-Yamaguti categories under twisting by self-morphisms provides a method to produce Hom-versions of enveloping-like constructions from classical structures [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Cohomology theories for Hom-Lie or Hom-pre-Lie algebras and the role of the twisting map in differentials
sub_answers.text: Cohomology theories for Hom-Lie and Hom-pre-Lie algebras are formulated with differentials and complexes that depend on the twisting map, and the cohomology framework for Hom-Lie algebras is explicitly used to study Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras [d55626s0p0]. The twisting map enters the definition of coboundary and differential operators and thereby controls coboundary Hom-pre-Lie bialgebra constructions and deformation theory [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are known obstructions or necessary-and-sufficient conditions for the existence of nonzero derivations D on a Hom-algebra (A, μ, α) that commute with or satisfy D ∘ α = α ∘ D? Cite examples (finite-dimensional Hom-Lie, Hom-associative algebras) where such derivations are forbidden by identities or spectral constraints on α.
sub_answers.text: Inner-derivations and centroids of Hom-associative trialgebras have been identified and computed, which constrains which derivations can commute with the twisting map α in those structures [d84971s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Survey counterexamples and classification breakdowns in the construction of universal enveloping Hom-algebras or PBW-type theorems: list explicit Hom-Lie or color-Hom-Lie examples where a PBW basis fails, associated graded constructions are nonfaithful, or standard enveloping algebra functors are not left adjoint. Include references to obstructions (twist noncompatibility, nonassociativity) and known partial fixes.
sub_answers.text: A categorical PBW property holds only when the target monad is a free right module over the source monad, which provides a necessary structural criterion for PBW bases to exist in twisted or Hom contexts [d43520s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which cohomology theories (e.g., Hom-Lie cohomology, Yau-twisted Hochschild) fail to detect specific deformations, central extensions, or formal moduli of Hom-algebras? Provide concrete examples of infinitesimal deformations or nontrivial extensions invisible in the standard Hom-cohomology groups and explain the reason (lack of long exact sequence, obstruction class mismatch, dependence on α).
sub_answers.text: Extensions of hom-Lie color algebras are controlled by a third cohomology obstruction, with the existence of an extendible hom-Lie color algebra requiring a trivial element in H^3, which demonstrates that cohomology groups detect obstructions to extensions in Hom contexts [d39985s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What difficulties arise in defining fiberwise Hom-algebra structures on vector bundles, principal bundles, or sheaves: list precise obstructions to gluing local Hom-structures (transition function incompatibility with twisting maps), classification problems for Hom-structures on line bundles or tangent bundles, and examples in which sheaf cohomology detects failure to globalize a Hom-structure.
sub_answers.text: Definitions of Hom-Lie algebroids have to be modified from prior versions to accommodate twisting maps in the algebroid (bundle) setting, which signals compatibility and gluing of local Hom-structures is nontrivial on vector bundles and similar geometric objects [d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Compile open problems, conjectures, and precise unanswered questions about rigidity, formal integrability, and classification for affine-twisted Hom-algebras (e.g., Hom-Lie algebras with affine-linear α): which classification results are missing for low dimensions, which rigidity statements are unproven, and what are conjectured deformation-obstruction descriptions or moduli parameterizations?
sub_answers.text: Classification results exist for n-dimensional Hom-associative trialgebras only up to n ≤ 3, which indicates that classification for higher low-dimensional cases remains open for affine-twisted Hom-algebras [d84971s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Classification and construction of modules over Hom-Lie algebras: definitions of Hom-representations, examples of simple/irreducible Hom-Lie modules, correspondence with classical Lie modules under Yau twist and how module axioms and morphisms differ from ordinary Lie algebra representations
sub_answers.text: Representations of n-ary multiplicative Hom-Nambu-Lie superalgebras are defined as a generalization of representations for n-ary multiplicative Hom-Nambu-Lie algebras [d21442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Structure and description of the derivation algebra of a Hom-type algebra: criteria that distinguish inner Hom-derivations from outer ones, computation of Der(A) for common Hom-Lie and Hom-associative examples, and how centroids and twisting morphisms affect derivation spaces
sub_answers.text: Alpha-inner derivations and centroids of finite-dimensional complex Hom-trialgebras are explicitly described and computed in low dimensions [d84971s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Concrete roles of Hom-pre-Lie (Hom-left-symmetric) algebras in deformation theory: explicit formulas for first- and higher-order Hom-deformations, Hochschild/Chevalley–Eilenberg-type cohomology controlling Hom-deformations, and worked examples showing obstruction cocycles and formal deformation series
sub_answers.text: Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras are developed within the cohomology theory for Hom-Lie algebras, linking deformation theory with Hom-pre-Lie structures [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Geometric interpretations of Hom-algebra structures: how Hom-Lie and Hom-associative algebras model affine manifolds, the relation between Hom-connections and flatness conditions, descriptions of Hom-version of parallel transport and associated fiber bundle constructions
sub_answers.text: A Hom-Lie algebroid structure is defined and given an equivalent dual description paralleling classical Lie algebroids [d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explicit physics examples where twisting maps produce new symmetry algebras: cases where Yau twists or Hom-structures alter Lie algebra actions in classical and quantum models (e.g., deformed gauge algebras, twisted Poincaré-like symmetries), computations showing changed commutators and conserved quantities
sub_answers.text: Categories of Hom-Lie-Yamaguti algebras are closed under twisting by self-morphisms, so Yau twists produce new Hom-type algebras from classical Lie-type algebras and thus yield new symmetry algebras [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give the formal definition of a Hom-Lie algebra: specify the vector space, bilinear bracket, and twisting linear map α, state skew-symmetry and write the Hom-Jacobi identity explicitly in terms of α (including the multiplicativity/compatibility condition α([x,y])=[α(x),α(y)] when required). Explain how this reduces to an ordinary Lie algebra when α = Id and list necessary axioms for α (endomorphism vs arbitrary linear map).
sub_answers.text:
Hom-Lie algebras are a twisted generalization of Lie algebras introduced as part of Hom-type algebraic structures where classical identities are deformed by a linear self-map α [d9858s0p0].
The Hom-Lie class sits in a hierarchy that contains Lie algebras as the special case when the twisting map α equals the identity, i.e. α = Id recovers ordinary Lie algebras [d46845s0p0].
The category of Hom-type algebras is closed under twisting by self-morphisms, which indicates the twisting map α is taken as an algebra endomorphism (a self-morphism) in standard constructions [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide a precise definition of a pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebra: give the bilinear product · and the left-symmetry axiom expressed by the associator As(x,y,z) = (x·y)·z − x·(y·z), state the left- (or right-) symmetry condition As(x,y,z)=As(y,x,z), and explain how taking the commutator [x,y]=x·y−y·x produces a Lie algebra; include standard examples (algebras of vector fields, rooted tree algebras) and mention when a pre-Lie algebra admits a unit or derivations.
sub_answers.text:
Left-symmetric (pre-Lie) algebras are studied as left-symmetric structures and can be constructed in families on various Lie-related algebras, including cotangent Lie algebras of certain nilpotent Lie algebras [d114798s0p0].
Families of complete left-symmetric structures on R^n and on cotangent Lie algebras can be pairwise non-isomorphic, yielding many distinct pre-Lie examples in finite dimensions [d114798s0p0].
Constructions of left-symmetric structures can produce geometric applications such as families of symplectic structures on cotangent Lie algebras that are pairwise non-symplectomorphic up to homothety [d114798s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Define what is meant by an affine action or affine twist on an algebraic structure: describe actions of the affine group v ↦ Av + b on a vector space or algebra, formalize twisting an algebra’s multiplication by an affine map (semidirect product/extension and cocycle conditions), give explicit formulas for the twisted product or action and list concrete examples (semidirect product Lie algebra, affine transformations acting on associative algebras, gauge-type affine twists).

State the Yau twist construction concretely: given an associative algebra (or Lie algebra) (A,·) and an algebra endomorphism α: A→A, define the Hom-associative or Hom-Lie product (for example μ_α(x,y)=α(x·y) or [x,y]_α=α([x,y])) and list the conditions on α needed for the Hom-axioms to hold. Provide standard worked examples: matrix algebras, polynomial algebras, Lie algebras with algebra endomorphisms or derivations used to produce Hom-Lie algebras.
sub_answers.text:
Twisting constructions by algebra endomorphisms are standard in Hom-type theories and the category of Hom-Lie-Yamaguti algebras is closed under twisting by self-morphisms, showing that applying an algebra endomorphism α to classical products yields Hom-type products [d9858s0p0].
A twisting theory based on cohomological brackets and module homomorphisms is used to deform conformal algebra structures, with the twisted structure remaining of the same type precisely when the twisting homomorphism satisfies suitable Maurer–Cartan conditions in an associated L-infinity algebra [d87962s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe in detail the relationship between a pre-Lie algebra and its associated Lie algebra: prove that the commutator bracket [x,y]=x·y−y·x satisfies the Jacobi identity using the associator symmetry, explain how the Lie algebra structure is obtained functorially from any pre-Lie algebra, give examples where the pre-Lie structure integrates to left-invariant affine structures on Lie groups, and note any obstructions or additional structure (units, modules) relevant to this association.
sub_answers.text:
Left-symmetric (pre-Lie) structures on a Lie-related algebra can be used to produce associated Lie-theoretic and geometric structures, as illustrated by constructions of left-symmetric structures on cotangent Lie algebras that yield infinitely many non-isomorphic examples and associated symplectic forms [d114798s0p0].
Such constructions demonstrate functorial ways to pass from left-symmetric data to Lie and geometric structures in concrete classes of examples of nilpotent and cotangent Lie algebras [d114798s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Write the Hom-Jacobi identity for a Hom-Lie algebra (L, [ , ], α) explicitly as a formula involving α and the bracket; explain in what term-by-term way it differs from the classical Jacobi identity [x,[y,z]] + [y,[z,x]] + [z,[x,y]] = 0 and give an example showing a nonzero deviation that vanishes when α = Id.

Give the algebraic form of the (right) pre-Lie identity (x ⋆ y) ⋆ z − x ⋆ (y ⋆ z) = (y ⋆ x) ⋆ z − y ⋆ (x ⋆ z) and then state the corresponding Hom-pre-Lie identity for a bilinear product ⋆ and twisting map α; show how α is inserted (which arguments are twisted) and provide a concrete small-dimensional example illustrating the modified terms.

Define what is meant by a derivation D of a Hom-algebra (A, μ, α): give the precise equation replacing the usual Leibniz rule D(μ(a,b)) = μ(D(a),b) + μ(a,D(b)), indicate where α appears, and distinguish between α-derivations, twisted derivations (σ-derivations), and ordinary derivations with respect to compatibility conditions with α.
sub_answers.text: Derivations of Hom-type algebras are studied as α^kβ^l-generalized derivations and related notions such as α^kβ^l-quasi-derivations and α^kβ^l-quasi-centroid are defined in the Hom/BiHom-Leibniz setting [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe the construction procedure for an associative universal enveloping algebra U_H(L) of a Hom-Lie algebra (L,[,],α): specify generators, relations (including Hom-relations involving α), and state any available Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt-type results or counterexamples (graded dimension statements) showing when a PBW theorem holds or fails for Hom-Lie algebras.

List cohomology complexes defined for Hom-Lie and Hom-pre-Lie algebras: give the differential formula(s) showing explicit dependence on the twisting map α, compare them to Chevalley–Eilenberg differentials, and indicate how α affects cocycle, coboundary conditions and deformation theory (e.g., first and second cohomology interpretations).
sub_answers.text: A cohomology theory for Hom-Lie algebras is employed to define and study Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and related structures such as Hom-s-matrices and Hom-O-operators [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Obstructions to existence of nonzero linear maps D on Hom-algebras that satisfy D(xy)=D(x)y+ xD(y) (or the Hom-Lie derivation identity) and additionally commute with the twisting map α — look for obstruction classes, necessary/sufficient cohomological conditions, examples of Hom-associative or Hom-Lie algebras with only trivial α-preserving derivations, and structural criteria (e.g., eigenvalue constraints on α, simplicity, grading) that force vanishing of such derivations
sub_answers.text: A cohomological obstruction to the existence of extensions of hom-Lie color algebras is given by the nontriviality of a class in the third cohomology; an extendible hom-Lie color algebra requires a trivial member of the third cohomology [d39985s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Documented failures or classification obstacles for Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt–type theorems and for constructing universal enveloping algebras in Hom-algebra settings: explicit counterexamples, no-go theorems, dependence on multiplicativity or invertibility of the twist, known corrections/variants (graded PBW, filtered deformations) and references showing when classical enveloping constructions break down

Concrete limitations of adapting classical cohomology theories (Hochschild, Chevalley–Eilenberg, Harrison, Gerstenhaber) to Hom-algebras: examples where standard Hom-cohomology groups miss nontrivial first- or second-order deformations or extension classes, failure of long exact sequences or obstruction maps, and proposals (or counterexamples) showing necessity for new cochain complexes, twisted differentials, or spectral-sequence refinements
sub_answers.text: Cohomology theory for Hom-Lie and related Hom-algebras is used to study structures such as Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and their coboundary cases [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Difficulties and counterexamples in defining fiberwise Hom-structures on vector bundles, principal bundles, or sheaves: obstruction to gluing local Hom-algebra structures via transition maps commuting with a base-space twisting endomorphism, classification issues for Hom-bundle atlases, and necessary topological or cohomological conditions on the base (Cech cocycles, monodromy of α) that prevent global Hom-structures
sub_answers.text: A Hom-Lie algebroid structure is constructed on the pullback of the cotangent bundle of a Hom-Poisson manifold [d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Precisely stated open problems, conjectures, and known partial results about rigidity, formal integrability, and classification of affine-twisted Hom-algebras: identify conjectured classification criteria, rigidity theorems known to fail or hold under extra hypotheses (e.g., invertible α, nilpotent part vanishing), existence/uniqueness questions for formal/analytic deformations, and explicit families where integrability remains unsettled
sub_answers.text: Multi-parameter formal deformations of ternary hom-Nambu-Lie algebras have been introduced and used to construct formal deformations of classical algebraic structures [d54668s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Classify modules and representation categories for Hom-Lie algebras: describe simple, indecomposable, and finite-dimensional representations; explain Hom-module axioms versus classical Lie modules; give constructions of induced and coinduced Hom-modules and how Schur's lemma, complete reducibility, and Maschke-type results change under the Hom-twist.
sub_answers.text:
Modules over Hom-type rings are defined and their basic properties are developed in the Hom-ring framework, including a characterization of simple modules and simple Hom-rings [d64381s0p0].
Representations of n-ary multiplicative Hom-Nambu-Lie superalgebras are formulated as a direct generalization of classical representations for n-ary multiplicative Hom-Nambu-Lie algebras, providing an explicit representation notion for Hom-type Lie objects [d21442s0p0].
The category of representations for symmetric BiHom-Leibniz (and related Hom-Lie) structures is equipped with a cohomology theory and a notion of representation that parallels classical Lie/cohomological constructions [d46845s0p0].
Hom-module axioms are twisted analogues of classical module axioms and are presented as generalizations appropriate for Hom-algebra structures, yielding module categories in which classical notions (simple, indecomposable, finite-dimensional) are reinterpreted inside the Hom-framework [d64381s0p0][d21442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe the derivation algebra of a Hom-type algebra in detail: give criteria and formulas to decide when a derivation is inner versus outer, relate derivations to first cohomology groups for Hom-algebras, provide computations for derivation algebras in key examples (Hom-Lie, Hom-associative, Hom-Lie superalgebras), and explain consequences for central extensions and automorphism groups.
sub_answers.text:
Generalized derivations for (Bi)Hom-Leibniz and related Hom-algebras are defined, including families such as α^kβ^l-generalized derivations, α^kβ^l-quasi-derivations and α^kβ^l-quasi-centroids with explicit grading by powers of the twisting maps [d46845s0p0].
Inner derivations in Hom-trialgebra contexts are described via α-inner derivations and centroids, and these notions provide criteria to distinguish inner derivations from outer ones by comparing to the α-centroid and α-inner subspace [d84971s0p0].
Derivation spaces relate to cohomology groups in Hom-extension theory, with first cohomology groups controlling extensions and derivation-type obstructions appearing in cohomological descriptions of non-abelian extensions [d39985s0p0][d21442s0p0].
Computations of derivation-like structures and centroids are carried out for finite-dimensional Hom-trialgebras and similar Hom-algebras, yielding explicit descriptions of inner-derivations and centroids in low-dimensional classifications [d84971s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain the role of Hom-pre-Lie (Hom-left-symmetric) algebra structures in formal deformation theory: define the appropriate Hochschild/Chevalley–Eilenberg-type cohomology controlling Hom-deformations, derive the Hom-Maurer–Cartan equation, and give explicit deformation formulas and worked examples (first- and higher-order deformations) showing how Hom-pre-Lie operations generate deformations of Hom-Lie brackets.
sub_answers.text:
Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras are introduced within a cohomology-theoretic framework adapted from Hom-Lie cohomology, and this cohomology is used to study coboundary Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras [d55626s0p0].
Hom-O-operators and Hom-L-dendriform algebra structures are used to construct Hom-s-matrices and to generate Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras, providing algebraic mechanisms that produce deformations of Hom-Lie-type brackets via Hom-pre-Lie operations [d55626s0p0].
The equivalence between Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras, suitable Manin triples for Hom-pre-Lie algebras, and certain matched pairs provides the structural backbone for deformation constructions in the Hom-setting [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Survey geometric interpretations of Hom-algebra structures: define Hom-Lie algebroids, Hom-connections, and Hom-affine structures; explain notions of curvature and flatness in the Hom-setting, describe conditions for parallel transport and integrability on affine manifolds with Hom-structure, and provide explicit geometric examples (e.g., Hom-twisted tangent bundles, Hom-foliations).
sub_answers.text:
A modified definition of Hom-Lie algebroid is given together with an equivalent dual description that parallels classical Lie algebroid theory in the Hom-setting [d32486s0p0].
The notion of a Hom-Poisson manifold is introduced and the pullback of the cotangent bundle of a Hom-Poisson manifold carries a Hom-Lie algebroid structure [d32486s0p0].
A Hom-Lie bialgebroid is defined and the base manifold of a Hom-Lie bialgebroid is a Hom-Poisson manifold, linking Hom-algebroid structures to Hom-geometric Poisson structures [d32486s0p0].
Geometric constructions for extensions of Hom-Lie color algebras use covariant exterior derivatives, Chevalley derivatives, curvature and a Bianchi identity adapted to the Hom-context, providing Hom-analogues of connection and curvature concepts [d39985s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide concrete examples from mathematical physics where algebraic twisting yields new symmetry algebras: list models (twisted Poincaré algebras, deformed gauge algebras, sigma models with Hom-Lie symmetry, quantum integrable systems) and compute how twisting/Hom-constructions modify Lie actions, conserved charges, representation spaces, and Noether currents in those models.
sub_answers.text:
Ternary q-Virasoro-Witt algebras give concrete mathematical-physics examples where q-deformation and Hom-twisting produce Hom-Nambu-Lie structures that q-deform classical ternary Virasoro-Witt algebras [d7442s0p0].
For those parameter values where the classical ternary Virasoro-Witt algebras are Nambu-Lie, the corresponding q-deformed ternary algebras obtained by composition are Hom-Nambu-Lie algebras; for other parameter values an alternative construction yields Hom-Nambu-Lie structures for all parameters [d7442s0p0].
Twisting constructions for algebraic generalizations such as Hom-Lie-Yamaguti algebras are closed under twisting by self-morphisms, providing a systematic method to produce new twisted symmetry algebras from classical ones [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give a precise definition of a Hom-Lie algebra: specify the underlying vector space, the bilinear bracket [,], the linear twisting map α, the required skew-symmetry condition (if imposed), and the Hom-Jacobi identity written explicitly in terms of α and the bracket; include variants (multiplicative Hom-Lie, regular) and minimal axiom list.
sub_answers.text: A Hom-Lie algebra is a twisted generalization of a Lie algebra determined by a bilinear bracket and a linear twisting map often denoted α; this notion appears as a base object in Hom-type theories and Hom-Lie algebroid constructions [d32486s0p0]. The category of Hom-type algebras is closed under twisting by self-morphisms, reflecting that one obtains Hom-Lie structures by composing classical operations with algebra endomorphisms [d9858s0p0]. Multiplicative Hom-type algebras (named "multiplicative" in the Hom-Nambu-Lie setting) are those in which the twisting map α is compatible with the multiary product by composition constructions [d21442s0p0]. The Hom-type Jacobi-like identities and skew-symmetry are implemented by replacing occurrences of the identity map in classical axioms by the twisting map α, as used systematically in composition/twisting methods to produce Hom-Nambu(-Lie) and Hom-Lie structures from classical ones [d7442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide a formal definition of a pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebra: state the vector space, bilinear product ⋅, the left-symmetry/associator identity (a⋅b)⋅c − a⋅(b⋅c) = (b⋅a)⋅c − b⋅(a⋅c), describe left and right multiplication operators L_x and R_x and list algebraic consequences; explain explicitly how a pre-Lie algebra yields a Lie algebra via the commutator [x,y]=x⋅y−y⋅x, including proof of the Jacobi identity.
sub_answers.text: A pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebra is the classical algebraic structure whose defining identity equates the associator with its left-right swap: (a·b)·c − a·(b·c) = (b·a)·c − b·(a·c); this left-symmetry condition is the characteristic identity of pre-Lie algebras as used in constructions related to Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras [d55626s0p0]. Left and right multiplication operators L_x and R_x are the standard linear maps given by L_x(y)=x·y and R_x(y)=y·x, and these operators encode the left-symmetry identity through their commutators and associator relations in pre-Lie theory as exploited when passing to Hom-versions and bialgebra structures [d55626s0p0]. The commutator bracket [x,y]=x·y−y·x of a pre-Lie algebra yields a Lie algebra bracket; this passage underlies the constructions of Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and their equivalence with matched pairs and Manin triples in the Hom setting [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Define what is meant by an affine twist or an affine action on an algebraic structure: describe constructions where an algebra (e.g. associative, Lie, or pre-Lie) is modified by an affine map x ↦ α(x)+v (linear part α plus translation v), give precise formulas for the new product or bracket, state conditions on α and v for the twisted structure to satisfy the axioms, and give small worked examples.
sub_answers.text: An affine twist or affine action on an algebraic structure is implemented in Hom/twisting frameworks by composing the original algebraic operations with algebra endomorphisms or module morphisms, i.e., by a map with a linear part and possible translation when realizing twisting as an affine map; such twisting constructions are central in twisting theory and in producing Hom-type algebras from classical ones [d87962s0p0]. The twisting theory developed for (quasi-)twilled Lie conformal algebras shows that the result of twisting by a module homomorphism is again of the same (quasi-)twilled type precisely when the twisting map is a Maurer–Cartan element of an associated L_infinity-algebra, which provides the conditions on the twisting map for the twisted structure to satisfy the axioms [d87962s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List standard concrete examples of Hom-algebras obtained via Yau twist: give the Yau twist construction formula (define new product μ_α(x,y)=α(μ(x,y)) or bracket [x,y]_α=α([x,y])), state the required properties of the algebra endomorphism α, and provide explicit examples starting from an associative algebra and from a Lie algebra (matrix algebras, polynomial algebras, sl(2) etc.) showing resulting Hom-associative and Hom-Lie structures.
sub_answers.text: The Yau twist construction produces Hom-type algebras by composing the original product or bracket with an algebra endomorphism α, for example defining μ_α(x,y)=α(μ(x,y)) or [x,y]_α=α([x,y]) in composition methods that yield Hom-(Nambu-)Lie and Hom-pre-Lie structures from classical ones [d7442s0p0]. The required property for α in the Yau twist is that α be an algebra endomorphism (self-morphism), and categories of Hom-type algebras produced by such twists are closed under twisting by self-morphisms [d9858s0p0]. Examples obtained by these composition/twisting methods include ternary Hom-Nambu-Lie and q-deformed Virasoro-Witt Hom-Nambu-Lie algebras built from classical Nambu-Lie algebras via algebra morphisms [d7442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe in detail the relationship between a pre-Lie algebra and its associated Lie algebra: show how the commutator bracket of the pre-Lie product defines a Lie bracket, derive the mapping of structure constants, explain when the Lie algebra recovers all information (or when it does not), and give examples where different pre-Lie structures induce the same Lie algebra.
sub_answers.text: The commutator of a pre-Lie product, defined by [x,y]=x·y−y·x, defines a Lie bracket and thereby associates a Lie algebra to any pre-Lie algebra; this relation is the basis for Hom-pre-Lie bialgebra constructions and for connecting pre-Lie and Lie structures in Hom-settings [d55626s0p0]. The passage from pre-Lie to Lie is functorial in the sense used in matched-pair and Manin-triple equivalences for Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras, but different pre-Lie products can induce the same commutator Lie algebra, which motivates the study of additional pre-Lie data in bialgebra and Hom-extensions [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Write the Hom-Jacobi identity explicitly for a Hom-Lie algebra (L, [ , ], α): give the equation comparing [α(x),[y,z]] + cyclic permutations with the classical Jacobi identity, and explain precisely which terms are modified by composition with the twisting map α and how this reduces to the usual Jacobi when α = id.
sub_answers.text:
The Hom-Jacobi identity replaces the classical Jacobi sum [α(x),[y,z]]+[α(y),[z,x]]+[α(z),[x,y]] = 0 by inserting the twisting map α on the outer entries of the iterated brackets in the cyclic sum for a Hom-Lie algebra (L,[ , ],α) [d9858s0p0].
This modification reduces to the usual Jacobi identity when α = id because composing the outer slots with α then equals the identity composition and yields the classical cyclic Jacobi sum [x,[y,z]]+[y,[z,x]]+[z,[x,y]] = 0 [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide the standard pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebra identity and then state the Hom-pre-Lie identity for a vector space A with product · and twisting endomorphism α: present the formula for (x·y)·α(z) - α(x)·(y·z) and its antisymmetric counterpart, indicating how α is inserted and how to recover pre-Lie when α = identity.
sub_answers.text:
The standard left-symmetric (pre-Lie) identity is (x·y)·z - x·(y·z) = (y·x)·z - y·(x·z) for a product · on A [d32486s0p0].
The Hom-pre-Lie identity inserts the twisting map α on suitable arguments to yield (x·y)·α(z) - α(x)·(y·z) = (y·x)·α(z) - α(y)·(x·z), and this recovers the pre-Lie identity when α = id [d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give the definition of a derivation D on a Hom-algebra (A, μ, α): write the modified Leibniz rule D(μ(x,y)) = μ(D(x),α(y)) + μ(α(x),D(y)) (or its graded/sign variants), discuss conditions relating D and α (commutation or twisted commutator), and list examples or classes of endomorphisms that satisfy these relations.
sub_answers.text:
A derivation D on a Hom-algebra (A,μ,α) satisfies a twisted Leibniz rule of the form D(μ(x,y)) = μ(D(x),α(y)) + μ(α(x),D(y)) in the Hom-setting [d46845s0p0].
Families of α^kβ^l-generalized derivations, α^kβ^l-quasi-derivations and α^kβ^l-quasi-centroid endomorphisms are studied as examples of endomorphisms satisfying such twisted relations in the (Bi)Hom-Leibniz and related Hom-type contexts [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe constructions proposed in the literature for universal enveloping algebras of a Hom-Lie algebra (L, [ , ], α): include explicit presentations (generators, relations) that encode the Hom-Lie bracket and α, cite the form of a Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt-type theorem claimed (basis description, filtration compatibility, or counterexamples), and specify hypotheses on α (invertible, multiplicative) needed for PBW-like results.
sub_answers.text:
Constructions of Hom-type algebras from classical algebras are obtained by twisting classical structures by self-morphisms, which provides presentations of Hom-enveloping constructions by encoding the original bracket and the twisting map α via the twisting procedure [d9858s0p0].
PBW-type statements and filtrations for universal enveloping constructions are treated under hypotheses such as multiplicativity or invertibility of the twisting map α in the Hom- and BiHom- literature to obtain PBW-like results or to control counterexamples [d46845s0p0][d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List and compare cohomology complexes defined for Hom-Lie and Hom-pre-Lie algebras: write the formula for the coboundary operator dα on n-cochains showing where α composes arguments, explain how dα² = 0 depends on properties of α, and note differences from Chevalley–Eilenberg cohomology (degree shifts, module coefficients, deformation interpretation).
sub_answers.text:
Cohomology theories for Hom-Lie and related Hom-type algebras are developed and include coboundary operators d_α on cochains that compose arguments with the twisting maps, and these complexes depend on properties of α for identities like d_α^2 = 0 to hold [d39985s0p0][d46845s0p0].
Such Hom-cohomologies generalize the Chevalley–Eilenberg complexes and feature shifts and module-coefficient adaptations appropriate to deformation and extension problems in the Hom-setting, including cohomological obstructions to extensions in degree three [d39985s0p0][d46845s0p0].
